examples.text: Er prahlt mit seinem neuen Auto.
examples.translation: He boasts about his new car.
examples.english: He boasts about his new car.

glosses: Faire le malin, fanfaronner, se vanter (de: mit + D).

examples.text: Er prahlt gern vor den anderen mit seinem Geld, mit seinen Beziehungen.
examples.translation: Il aime bien se vanter de son argent, de ses relations devant les autres.

examples.text: Im dreckigen, feuchten Sand am Fuß einer Rutsche, die so verrostet ist, dass Eltern ihre Kinder aus Angst vor Tetanus nicht mehr darauf setzen, kippen sie die Flasche Cognac hinunter; und nachdem Eduard sich zunächst ein bisschen dafür geschämt hat, prahlt er nun damit, ins Büro des Direktors geschissen zu haben.
examples.translation: Assis dans le sable sale et humide, au pied d’un toboggan si rouillé que les parents évitent d’y amener les petits de peur qu’ils n’attrapent le tétanos, ils assèchent au goulot la bouteille de cognac et, après en avoir eu un peu honte, Édouard finit par se vanter d’avoir chié dans le bureau du directeur.

examples.text: Studien zum Thema (Untreue) beruhen größtenteils auf Selbstauskünften der Probanden – und hier neigen Männer dazu, mit ihren Affären zu prahlen und zu übertreiben, während Frauen sich sittsamer geben, als sie sind.
examples.translation: Les études sur le sujet (de l'infidélité) se basent en grande partie sur les déclarations des sujets eux-mêmes - et là, les hommes ont tendance à se vanter et à exagérer leurs aventures, tandis que les femmes se montrent plus pudiques qu’elles ne le sont.

examples.text: Du willst wohl mit deinem neuen Auto prahlen?

glosses: A boast or boasting; bragging; ostentatious pretence or self-glorification.

examples.text: Caesar […] made not here his brag / Of "came", and "saw", and "overcame".

glosses: The thing which is boasted of.

examples.text: Beauty is Nature's brag.

You could just use ordinary shop-bought kecap manis to marinade the meat, but making your own is easy, has a far more elegant fragrance and is, above all, such a great brag! Flavouring kecap manis is an intensely personal thing, so try this version now and next time cook the sauce down with crushed, split lemongrass and a shredded lime leaf.
our mixed companies here, which, if they happen to rise above bragg and whist, infallibly stop short of every thing either pleasing or instructive

glosses: To boast; to talk with excessive pride about what one has, is able to do, or has done; often as an attempt to popularize oneself.

examples.text: to brag of one’s exploits, courage, or money
Conceit, more rich in matter than in words, / Brags of his substance, not of ornament. / Nor shall Death brag thou wander’st in his shade

glosses: Brisk; full of spirits; boasting; pretentious; conceited.

examples.text: a woundy, brag young fellow
Seest how brag yond bullock beare […]his pricked eares?

translations.source_sense_description: intransitiv: sich übertrieben oder unangemessen loben

glosses: To exhibit the best attributes of something.

examples.text: Grocery stores show off their produce by placing the most attractive specimens in front.

glosses: To attract attention to for the purpose of bragging or personal exhibitionism; to demonstrate a skill, talent or property for the purpose of bragging or personal exhibitionism.

examples.text: She loves to show off her driving prowess.
She loves to show off when she gets behind the wheel of a car.

“Listen, my Oscar,” she said, resuming at once her tender voice, “you have a propensity to talk, and to tell all you know, and all that you don’t know; and you do it to show off, with the foolish vanity of a mere lad.[…]”

If you've just acquired a Google Glass headset for £1,000, don't show it off at the movies. UK cinemas are to ban the headsets over fears that the gadgets can be used to make pirate copies of Hollywood blockbusters.
She told the press that the group had been for an evening out and that the driver has been showing off by driving fast.
